t:
(a) 
In General.—
The Special Representative shall coordinate the consideration of international trade policy issues that arise as a result of, and shall develop international trade policy as it relates to, the implementation of this title.
 
    (b) 
Negotiating Functions.—
The Special Representative has responsibility for coordinating United States discussions and negotiations with foreign countries for the purpose of establishing mutual arrangements with respect to standards-related activities. In carrying out this responsibility, the Special Representative shall inform and consult with any Federal agency having expertise in the matters under discussion and negotiation.
 
    (c) 
Cross Reference.—
For provisions of law regarding general authority of the Special Representatives with respect to trade agreements, see section 111 of the Trade Act of 197 1(19 U.S.C. 2171).

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the words "coordinate" and "consult" signal participation, but the only consultation required is with Federal agencies, which is intra-government coordination. The negotiations with foreign countries are diplomatic dealings aimed at international arrangements, not a process that brings outside parties into a federal decision. The section sets up no public comment, hearing, advisory body with non-federal members, or right to sue.
fable.s: the Special Representative shall inform and consult with any Federal agency having expertise in the matters under discussion and negotiation

opus.w: The only consultation the section requires is with federal agencies, which is coordination inside the government and is not participation. Negotiating with foreign countries is the federal government carrying out diplomacy itself, not outside parties being consulted before a federal decision. The section has no public comment, hearing, advisory body with outside members, or consultation with states or tribes.
opus.s: In carrying out this responsibility, the Special Representative shall inform and consult with any Federal agency having expertise in the matters under discussion and negotiation.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The section mentions "negotiations with foreign countries," and foreign governments are outside the U.S. federal government. It also requires the Special Representative to "consult." That could look like outside participation.

   **Why it fails:** The consultation runs only to "any Federal agency having expertise," so it is coordination inside the government. Negotiating with foreign countries is the federal government's own diplomatic work, not outsiders being consulted before a federal decision. No states, tribes, experts, companies, or members of the public are brought in, and the section has no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Special Representative (a federal official) to consult with other Federal agencies. According to the definition, consultation or coordination between federal agencies or federal officials is intra-government coordination and is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation. No outside parties (states, tribes, public, companies, etc.) are involved in this specific consultation process.
qwen_chat.s: In carrying out this responsibility, the Special Representative shall inform and consult with any Federal agency having expertise in the matters under discussion and negotiation.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: The text mentions "consult with any Federal agency," which might suggest participation. However, the definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination *between* federal agencies or federal officials is intra-government coordination and does **not** count as participation. Since the Special Representative is a federal official and the agencies consulted are federal agencies, this interaction stays entirely inside the federal government.
